# Gramlot 0.3.0 — Components, forms and validation

Gramlot now provides reusable web components authored with the same names and
parameters from Python and JavaScript. Explicit collections pair a browser module
with generated Builder metadata; the core retains Source/Data ownership.

- Seventeen inputs, shared labelbox, reactive label/style parameters, typed numeric,
  date and time editors, local/callback choices and a date picker.
- Formlet automatically aligns labels by column; groupBox copies accepted Data as
  TYTX or JSON. Checkbox supports switch mode and a reactive switch color.
- Built-in button, LED toggle and unified dropdown; html_button remains plain HTML.
- Field validation retains invalid drafts and the last valid Data, supports local
  rules, transformations, conditions, warnings, callbacks and asynchronous RPC.
- Mimi/Joanna themes, touch presentation and page device metadata; inspector enum
  editors and clearer calendar/property controls.
- Shared Builder pointer grammar removes duplicate consumer parsing. Transforms use
  : / :=; legacy automatic ${name} templates are not supported.

Upgrade the core, examples and hosting packages together and rebuild source-checkout
browser assets. See the update and component guides in the public manual. DB/grid
validation, stores, full form persistence and translation services remain separate.

Qualification: 3,544 JS tests; 146 Python tests with one existing expected upstream
failure; Chromium/WebKit component and cross-host gallery checks; clean wheel/npm
installs and strict documentation checks. Firefox could not launch in the local
verification environment and is not claimed as qualified for these new controls.
